column3: A campfire at night on 128x64: a crackling fire in the middle with logs, two kids on logs either side holding sticks over the flames, a starry sky and pine silhouettes. The time is marshmallows: each numeral is a marshmallow (or a stack of them) on a stick, toasting from white to golden to brown as the minute passes (design puffy marshmallow numerals). Always alive: flames dance with real fire colour, sparks rise, embers glow, faces flicker in the firelight, an owl blinks. Minute turn: the old marshmallow catches fire, the kid panics and blows it out, eats it (cheeks bulge), and skewers a fresh white one with the new numeral. Hour: a shooting star, s'mores are made, the fire flares.

A Grand Prix race along the 256x64 banner: side view of fast racing cars on a track with kerbs, grandstands and sponsor boards streaming by in parallax. The time is the race order: four cars carry the four numerals as their big race numbers (design bold livery numerals), holding position in HH:MM order; a timing board up top. Always alive: wheels spin, cars jostle and draft, heat haze, tyre smoke, the crowd waves flags. Minute turn: a car with the new number dives down the inside and overtakes the old one, which drops back and peels off into the pits. Hour: a pit stop, the crew swarms the car, the chequered flag waves.

A brick wall in a city alley on 192x64 at night under a streetlamp. The time is graffiti: wildstyle spray-paint numerals with fat outlines, 3D drop shadows, highlights, drips and overspray (design the tag letterforms). A writer in a hoodie (bold silhouette) sprays with a can, mist puffing. Always alive: the lamp flickers, a cat walks the wall top, paint drips run slowly, steam from a grate. Minute turn: a council worker rolls grey paint over the old digit with a roller, and the writer sprays the new one outline-first then fill, the can rattling. Hour: a crew paints a full piece in a burst of colour and they flee as a torch beam sweeps.

A pachinko machine, 64x128 tall: a vertical field of brass pins with silver balls cascading through, flashing lights, a central LCD that shows the time in a flashy anime-style numeral reel (design it), and win pockets that light up. Always alive: a steady stream of balls falls and bounces off the pins (real bounce physics, sub-pixel), lights chase around the frame, the reel idles with sparkles. Minute turn: a ball drops into the start pocket, the reel spins with a reach-animation suspense build, and lands on the new minute with a fanfare and a ball payout cascade. Hour: fever mode, the whole frame flashes and balls flood the tray.

Watercolour painting on one 64x64 panel: wet paper texture (subtle grain), and a brush that paints the time in watercolour: pigment pools at the edges of each stroke, blooms (backruns) spread where wet meets wet, colours bleed into each other, and the paint dries slowly lighter. Design brush numerals painted stroke by stroke in two or three harmonious colours. Always alive: wet areas glisten and slowly spread, a drop falls from the brush and blooms, the light shifts across the paper. Minute turn: a wet sponge lifts the old digit (leaving a faint ghost stain), and the brush paints the new one with visible wet edges that dry over seconds. Hour: a wash of colour floods the whole sheet and is blotted away.

A 1950s jukebox, 128x192 portrait: chrome arch with bubbling coloured tubes, a lit glass dome showing the record carousel and the tone arm, a title-strip selector panel with the time on it as the selected record (design chrome-and-neon numerals), speaker grille at the bottom. Always alive: bubbles rise in the tubes, colours cycle through the arch, the record spins, the grille glows with the beat, a dancing couple's silhouette maybe. Minute turn: a coin drops, the carousel rotates and the mechanism lifts a new 45 onto the turntable, the selector flips to the new minute, the arm lands. Hour: the lights go wild and the whole cabinet pulses.
